summary: Clarify behavior when client cancels request but server-side tool executes; retry semantics and visibility of side effects
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that when their client cancels an in-flight streaming request (HTTP client disconnect / CancelToken), they sometimes see the downstream tool webhook invoked on Redwood side even though the client received a cancel. They are unclear whether retries or server-side resubmits are occurring, and want guidance on guarantee semantics and how to observe side-effect invocations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Using Python SDK, open a streaming chat session with a function/tool configured that performs an external webhook POST (customer's webhook).

2) Trigger a prompt that will cause the model to call the tool, then immediately cancel the client request (client.close() or CancelToken) during the streaming response chunk where function_call is emitted but before final ack from client.
3) Observe that the customer's webhook occasionally receives the POST after the client has already disconnected and shows duplicated payloads when client retries the user-side request.
4) Repeat with TS SDK and with the same API key from a different host to rule out local client retry logic.
logs: Request-id: rq_8c1a2d3b - initial stream open - server saw 'client_disconnect' at 2026-03-12T15:04:12Z
Serving-runtime trace: span=serve-evict-iat id=span_22c - function_call routed to tool-runner queue 3 at 2026-03-12T15:04:12.120Z
Tool-runner log: tool-invoke id=tr_9f4 - POST to https://hooks.nimbusp.example/internal/pay at 2026-03-12T15:04:12.145Z - 200 OK
Client retry: local app attempted resend at 2026-03-12T15:04:13Z (non-Redwood retry middleware)
observed_behavior: Customer sees external webhook POSTs from Redwood after their client cancelled. In some cases the webhook receives duplicate calls when the customer-side client retries the user request after reconnecting.
expected_behavior: When a client cancels an in-flight request, Redwood should not silently retry/duplicate tool invocations. If a tool invocation has already been accepted by the serving-runtime and dispatched to the tool-runner, it may complete independently of the client's socket; we should document this and provide visibility hooks and recommended patterns to avoid duplicates.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: client cancel occurs after serving-runtime has enqueued the tool-runner job; job runs to completion and is independent of the client socket lifecycle.
Found serving-runtime trace showing 'enqueue-to-tool' happened within 25ms of client disconnect; tool-runner accepted and executed the POST (see logs).

Observed customer app was performing an automatic retry on reconnect which caused a second logical request to be sent (client-side), generating another tool invocation because there was no idempotency key in the payload.

Confirmed Python SDK default streaming implementation does not attach request-scoped idempotency token for function/tool calls; SDKs currently expose idempotency guidance but do not auto-populate for streaming cancellations.
Related dashboards: /dashboards/requests/streaming-tool-exec (shows spike at 2026-03-12T15:04 UTC for customer API key).
Slack thread: #support-nimbus (link: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C07xxxx/p167xx) contains initial customer logs and a short video of the reproduce.

Checked for server-side automatic retry: no retry policy configured for tool-runner queue 3 (confirmed in scheduler config), so duplicates are primarily from multiple user-initiated requests rather than internal retries.
comments: Priya Rao (Support): Posted initial reproduce and logs, asked for SRE confirmation on enqueue semantics.

Liam O'Connor (SRE): Confirmed serve->enqueue->tool-runner flow is asynchronous; once enqueued, tool-runner processes regardless of client socket. Recommended documenting that tool side-effects may outlive client connection and advising idempotency keys.
Customer (Engineer, NimbusPay): Reports they rely on at-most-once semantics for billing webhook; asked for recommended mitigation while we provide guidance.
Product (Elena Kim): Requested proposal for SDK change: attach optional 'tool_idempotency' header/token for streaming sessions and add console toggle to surface tool-runner events per-request.

Support (Priya): Shared temporary workaround: include application-level idempotency token in 'tool_call.metadata' JSON field and ensure the webhook checks/returns 409 if duplicate. Also suggested using unique idempotency tokens derived from user action id.
root_cause: Combination of asynchronous tool-run execution (serve enqueues job before client cancel) and lack of client-generated idempotency tokens for streaming function calls. Customer-side automatic retry on reconnect caused a second logical request leading to duplicate tool invocations.
resolution: Workaround provided to customer: 1) Add a per-user-action idempotency token into tool_call.metadata and have the tool webhook deduplicate (idempotency key). 2) For streaming flows, have the client attach a deterministic idempotency token in initial request headers to be stored in the runtime trace for correlation. Long-term: engineering to add optional SDK helper that emits an idempotency token header for streaming sessions and Console to show tool-runner events for each request.
next_steps: ENG-PLATFORM: Implement SDK helper (python/ts) to generate and attach 'X-RW-Tool-Idempotency' for streaming sessions (backlog), link: GH-PR-available
ENG-RUNTIME: Expose tool-runner event visibility in Console and add ability to surface 'tool-invoked' per-request (low-risk feature).
DOCS: Update 'Streaming & Function Calls' doc to explicitly call out that tool invocations may complete after client cancellation and recommend idempotency patterns.
CS: Follow up with customer on 2026-03-16 to validate workaround and confirm duplicated calls stop.
